content:
Retired conservative federal judge J. Michael Luttig on Monday warned that Donald Trump is increasingly becoming "cornered" and likely feeling "besieged on all sides."

Appearing on Nicolle Wallace's MS NOW show, the jurist — appointed by George H.W. Bush, who has become a prominent Trump critic — compared the president to a trapped wild animal, saying the situation should concern America and the world.

Luttig pointed to mounting pressures, from the cost-of-living crisis to the seemingly endless war in Iran, and said he believes the opposition to the president is intensifying. "We all knew this day would come. We knew it six years ago. We knew it for the last 19 or 20 months. And we know it today — that Donald Trump, the president of the United States, is cornered," he said.

Luttig added that Trump "feels besieged,"

and said: "Like a trapped wild animal," adding that "today, this week, he is desperate," and "will remain desperate from now until the midterm elections and through the inauguration of the new Congress in January."

"He is desperate like a trapped animal," Luttig added.

Luttig, who advised then-Vice President Mike Pence in 2021 when Trump tried to overturn his 2020 election loss to Joe Biden, said Trump's problem now is that "he is being cornered by America itself and everything America has always stood for."

He added: "For 250 years, America has been the envy of the world, a global beacon of freedom and human rights — until Trump became president, after which America is no longer that." He went on to say Trump has "attacked everything about America."

But he said "America is now pushing back," and "the walls are closing in on him, and he is desperate at this moment. That should worry all of us, and it should worry the world."

Wallace lightened the ominous tone with humor, joking: "I'm picturing more of a manatee than a cheetah as the trapped wild animal."
